correctness.rationale: An independent C++17 finite enumerator rebuilt the Kneser vertices as unordered pairs and all closed signatures using disjointness; it counted every increasing k-subset, k=1,...,6 (499177 candidates total for K(8,2) and 2391495 for K(9,2)). Every k<6 subset fails identification; exactly 141120 and 7560 six-subsets pass. Full one-removal/one-addition adjacency yields edges 4730880 and 22680. For K(8,2) BFS produces one component and exact degree multiplicities 56:3360, 58:10080, 64:20160, 66:67200, 72:10080, 74:30240. For K(9,2) BFS gives 280 components each of 27 degree-six codes. Separately, the source constructive certificate enumerates 280 partitions of nine elements into triples and 3^3 center choices, all yielding spanning 3P3 identifying codes and all 7560 optimal codes; changing one path edge moves only one center, so each component is K3□K3□K3. Complete finite exhaustive searches prove exactly the stated finite orders and do not extrapolate to other n.
